site.name: SMILE Research Group
site.description: The Software Maintenance and Intelligent Evolution (SMILE) Research Group at the University of Michigan–Flint develops intelligent methods to help developers understand, test, refactor, and evolve software systems.
site.heroImageAlt: SMILE researchers and collaborators at the ASE 2022 organizing committee

researchAreas.title: Software maintenance and evolution
researchAreas.description: Methods that help developers understand and safely evolve complex software systems.

researchAreas.title: Refactoring and software quality
researchAreas.description: Evidence-driven approaches to improving software design, maintainability, and quality.

researchAreas.title: Automated software engineering
researchAreas.description: Intelligent and search-based techniques for testing, analysis, and software engineering tasks.

researchAreas.title: Model-driven engineering
researchAreas.description: Models and tools that support the design, analysis, and evolution of software-intensive systems.

teamLead.name: Mohamed Wiem Mkaouer
teamLead.role: Professor of Computer Science · Principal Investigator
teamLead.biography: Mohamed Wiem Mkaouer leads SMILE and is a Professor of Computer Science in the College of Innovation and Technology at the University of Michigan–Flint. His research connects software engineering and artificial intelligence.
